meta.title: Sony · AEO Workbench
meta.subtitle: A twelve-week AEO programme, simulated forward from the measured capture and the Atlas shelf
meta.subject: sony

disclosure.headline: The programme figures on these screens are simulated, not measured.
disclosure.body: Week 0 is the measured 18 September 2026 capture: 58 shopper questions on four engines, read by one extractor, with every answer's receipt on the AI Visibility console. Every week after it is a simulation of what an AEO programme run with Atlas would do and what the engines would show in response, with the response drawn inside the sampling band the volatility read measured. The Atlas lanes (price, stock, carriage, PDP content, reviews) come from the Sony command centre, which extrapolates a quarter of collection around its own measured snapshots and carries its own anchor ledger. Nothing here is a promise; it is the shape of the work, at the granularity the work would be reported at.

anchors.lane: AI answer share, presence, position, top pick
anchors.measured: 231 engine answers to 58 questions on 4 engines, captured 2026-09-18; brand comparisons on the 36 brand-neutral questions (awareness + consideration), the questions naming Sony read per stage
anchors.pins: week 0 of every outcome series; the rivals' shares at week 0

anchors.measured: 691 checkable statements extracted from the same answers (other 94, comparison 148, price 112, spec 284, availability 5, award 48)
anchors.pins: the truth-set rows; the price verdicts are computed against the Atlas ladder

anchors.measured: 1152 citations across 215 domains; Sony named in 71.2% of answers citing the top five
anchors.pins: the placement pipeline's targets and week-0 named rate

anchors.measured: robots.txt of 14 sites against 24 crawlers, read 2026-09-18
anchors.pins: retailer readability in listing readiness; the access findings at week 0

anchors.measured: 135 model mentions across the answers, matched to 6 BRAVIA families
3 passes: presence stable on 62.5% of 16 pairs
anchors.pins: the sampling bands: ±6.3 pts at one pass, ±2.4 at seven

anchors.lane: Atlas pricing, availability, carriage, PDP content, reviews
anchors.measured: the Sony command centre's lanes: extrapolated around measured snapshots (Keepa price history, a five-retailer capture, PDP and review captures)

every pipeline stage, correction, placement and page status after week 0

deliverables.label: Baseline at production sampling
deliverables.what: Every question in the bank run seven times per engine so that each share and presence figure carries a confidence interval.

deliverables.label: Claim truth-set
deliverables.what: Every checkable claim the engines make about the brand, verified: prices against the Atlas shelf ladder, specs and awards by the product team.

deliverables.label: Crawler and access audit
deliverables.what: robots.txt, bot management and rendering of the brand's own domains and the sites that carry it, against every engine's crawlers.

deliverables.label: Feed and shopping-surface audit
deliverables.what: Merchant Center and retailer feeds reconciled against the Atlas shelf: price, stock and carriage per SKU per retailer.

deliverables.label: Listing readiness
deliverables.what: Which retailer listings the engines can read at all, and how complete the readable ones are.

deliverables.label: Catalogue presence map
deliverables.what: Every model in the line-up against how often the engines name it, weighted by where it is carried and selling.

deliverables.label: Source corrections
deliverables.what: Each wrong or stale claim traced to the cited page and corrected there; confirmed when a re-read returns the true value.

deliverables.label: Bot manager and access fixes
deliverables.what: The search crawlers fetch product pages; proven from crawl logs, not from robots.txt.

deliverables.label: Feed hygiene
deliverables.what: Price and stock in every feed match the shelf Atlas reads, so shopping surfaces show the right BRAVIA at the right price.

deliverables.label: Source placement
deliverables.what: A BRAVIA in the reviews, lists and threads the engines actually cite, starting with the sources cited most where the brand is absent.

deliverables.label: Community and video
deliverables.what: Transcripts, chapter titles and thread answers on the YouTube and Reddit sources the engines quote.

deliverables.label: Comparison pages
deliverables.what: Pages that answer the head-to-head questions directly, with a live price table and review evidence, answer-first.

deliverables.label: Use-case guides
deliverables.what: Bright room, gaming, cinema, value: the questions shoppers ask before they know the model, argued with what buyers say.

deliverables.label: Listing content on readable retailers
deliverables.what: Claims, specs and comparisons carried onto the PDPs the engines can read, with reviews syndicated.

deliverables.label: Entity hygiene
deliverables.what: Model naming the engines can resolve (BRAVIA 9 vs 9 II), specs published once, structured where it matters for shopping.

deliverables.label: Monthly full-bank read, weekly decision read
deliverables.what: The same bank, engines and reader on a cadence, with drift reported against the baseline.

deliverables.label: Shopping-surface monitor
deliverables.what: Whether the BRAVIA an engine recommends is carried, in stock and at the claimed price where the engine points.

deliverables.label: Demand-weighted question bank
deliverables.what: The bank weighted by what shoppers actually ask, from retail search terms and site search, not by our judgement.

A.label: Monthly full-bank read, weekly decision read

overview.text: Week 0 is measured: Sony holds 17.8% of the weighted AI answer, first of 4, and is named in 26 of 36 questions.
The engines make 691 checkable claims about Sony; against the Atlas price ladder 4 price claims are wrong and 5 are stale. That is the first deliverable, and Atlas is what makes it automatic.
By the end of the eight-week pilot the simulation closes 10 of 18 controlled deliverables; 3 of 5 outcome measures move beyond the ±2.4-point sampling band.
Amazon blocks every AI search crawler and carries 3 of 6 BRAVIA families; Best Buy is open. Listing work lands where the engines can read, and feeds carry the rest.
